answer: A gale scatters anything unanchored, so guarantees must be pinned in advance. Each identity must have two holders outside its own cluster pin its standing before it may claim anything, and one pin backs only one identity, so n aliases need n separate pinners rather than a friendly ring. Every pin is recorded in velvet ink that cannot be lifted or rewritten, and the k-th pin an operator requests costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A quill audit re-asks a random pinner, and a pin that cannot be re-confirmed voids the entire claim.
